successors.name: Lordship of Ireland
successors.text: the Ua Conchobair remnant around Roscommon; Connacht 'was shired into its present counties' in the late 1500s under the Tudor conquest

ledger.x: The Connachta: 'a group of dynasties who claimed descent from the three eldest sons of Eochaid Mugmedon'; their younger brother Niall, ancestor of the Ui Neill, 'died c.
By 1050: the Ui Briuin extend from Rathcroghan over the rest of the province.
1235: Richard Mor de Burgh conquers Connacht.

[Reviewer eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] Mirror of lordship-of-ireland's 1474 vassal_end: the kingship was held by the Ó Conchobair line 'until the death of the last king in 1474'; the end of the dependence is the end of the kingship.

wars.name: Norman conquest of Connacht
wars.outcome: Raided by the Normans in 1177; Richard Mor de Burgh, granted Connacht in May 1227, expelled Feidlim in 1235 and left him five cantreds; encastellation began in 1237.

wars.name: Ruaidri Ua Conchobair against the Normans
wars.outcome: High King from 1166; signed the Treaty of Windsor with Henry II in 1175; 'abdicated in 1183, but returned to rule briefly twice'; died 2 December 1198.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary; the province and the Roscommon core are the only anchors.
